resources.string: Pluto Keyboard is based on FUTO Keyboard by FUTO. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by FUTO.

Pluto Keyboard is a private keyboard that works without an internet connection. On top of FUTO Keyboard, it adds live voice typing, automatic punctuation, Smart corrections for dictation, and keys that adapt to how you type.
This is a modified version of FUTO Keyboard. FUTO\'s copyright and license (FUTO Source First License 1.1) still apply to the FUTO Keyboard code.

Get the voice typing model, plus optional punctuation and Smart corrections

These models are English only for now, because Moonshine only understands English. Pluto has no internet access, so it can\'t download models by itself. Tap Download to get a file in your browser, then come back here, tap Import and choose the file you downloaded.
Recommended. Turns your speech into text as you talk. Other sizes are on the voice model page (Languages & Models → English → Voice Input Model).
Moonshine puts a period at almost every pause. This model replaces its punctuation with real sentences, commas and capital letters after you stop speaking.

Reads each finished dictation with a small language model and fixes what only the whole sentence can tell, like misheard words (“bulls” → “bowls”, “their” → “there”) and names and words from your personal dictionary. You can also turn on numbers as digits, voice commands like “new paragraph”, filler word removal, self-correction fixes, quotation marks and emoji by name. It never rephrases what you said and adds up to about two seconds after you stop speaking.

Catches typos that slip past autocorrect, using the words around them.

Rereads each sentence you finish and fixes the typos that slipped through, using the words around them. Choose which kinds below. Tap the undo button above the keyboard to change a fix back. Undoing teaches it to be more careful there, and fixing a miss yourself builds its confidence. English only.
Fix typos that are real words
Catches slips that spell another word, like “salt an pepper” or “an email form my boss”, once the rest of the sentence makes it clear. Uses the typing corrections list.

When a misspelled word slips through, say because it was the middle suggestion so the space bar kept it, this works out the word you meant from the letters you typed and the sentence around them, like “ststy the game” → “start the game”. It only steps in when one word is the clear answer. Your own words, names and abbreviations are left alone.
